past_medical_history: Prostate cancer, Gleason 6 (3+3), diagnosed 2018, on active surveillance — PSA stable 3.2 ng/mL

medications.frequency: as needed up to 3 times daily

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue fasciculations. No dysarthria. Jaw jerk brisk.
neurological_exam.motor: Right leg weakness — foot drop, right tibialis anterior 3/5. Left leg 4/5 overall. Bilateral arm fasciculations. Right thenar wasting with fasciculations.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Knee jerks 3+ bilateral. Biceps 3+ bilateral. Hoffmans bilateral. Bilateral Babinski positive.
neurological_exam.coordination: Normal in arms. Right leg coordination mildly impaired due to foot drop.
neurological_exam.gait: Right foot drop — steppage gait. Spastic quality bilaterally.
neurological_exam.additional: Prostate cancer history requires exclusion of spinal metastasis, but PSA stable and no back pain.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive right leg weakness and foot drop over 12 months; right hand twitching
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. W is a 72-year-old retired insurance adjuster with a history of low-grade prostate cancer on active surveillance who presents with a 12-month history of progressive right leg weakness and foot drop. He first noticed difficulty lifting his right foot approximately 12 months ago, initially thinking he had sprained his ankle. However, no ankle injury was documented and the weakness has steadily worsened without any mechanism of injury. Over the following months, he developed bilateral arm fasciculations that his wife noticed during dinner, and he reports progressive weakness of his right hand making it difficult to open jars and turn door handles. He has no back pain, no bowel or bladder dysfunction, and no sensory loss in any distribution. His prostate cancer has been under active surveillance with stable PSA at 3.2 ng/mL — he has had no bone scan or CT suggesting metastatic disease. His oncologist performed imaging 8 months ago that showed no evidence of metastatic disease. He denies any new urinary symptoms that would suggest new cord compression. The neurological symptoms have progressed in a relentless ascending pattern and he has had no plateaus or episodes of recovery.

findings.location: Bilateral corticospinal tracts — posterior limb internal capsule, cerebral peduncles

signal_characteristics.T2: No epidural mass, no cord compression, no leptomeningeal enhancement, no vertebral marrow replacement lesion

additional_observations: No lytic or blastic vertebral lesions — metastatic prostate cancer to spine excluded
No cord compression — prostate metastatic myelopathy excluded
Mild degenerative facet changes — no significant foraminal stenosis at L4-L5 or L5-S1 to explain foot drop
Normal lumbar spine — L4-L5 disc bulge mild without nerve root compression
mri.impression: Importantly, no evidence of spinal metastases or cord compression from prostate cancer. Mild L4-L5 degenerative changes insufficient to explain the clinical picture of progressive bilateral weakness with UMN signs. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Tongue: fibrillations +1, fasciculations. Consistent with early bulbar LMN involvement.
Right FDI: fibrillations +2, large MUPs. Right APB: fibrillations +1. Bilateral paraspinals C5-C7: fibrillations +1.

Right tibialis anterior: fibrillations +3, positive sharp waves +3, markedly reduced recruitment — consistent with foot drop. Left tibialis anterior: fibrillations +1. Right gastrocnemius: fasciculations. Lumbosacral paraspinals L3-L5: fibrillations +1. NOTE: paraspinal denervation CANNOT be caused by L4-L5 foraminal stenosis (paraspinals innervated by posterior primary rami — proximal to foramen).
Peroneal, sural, median: NORMAL. No sensory neuropathy — confirms pure motor involvement.
Right peroneal motor: CMAP amplitude 1.4 mV (markedly reduced; reference >2 mV), normal conduction velocity 44 m/s. No conduction block.

quantitative_data.classification: Definite ALS by El Escorial and Awaji criteria
quantitative_data.note: Paraspinal denervation at lumbosacral level excludes lumbar disc/foraminal disease as explanation for foot drop

specialized_test.impression: Definite ALS. Right foot drop is due to lumbosacral motor neuron degeneration, not L4-L5 disc disease — paraspinal denervation and bilateral upper motor neuron signs confirm this. Lumbar disc disease is an incidental finding.
recommended_actions: ALS confirmed. Riluzole. ALS MDC. PFT. Ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) for foot drop management.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: SNIP 68 cmH2O (L), NIF -52 cmH2O (H).

interactions: Tamsulosin: no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction with riluzole
warnings: Monthly LFT monitoring for riluzole hepatotoxicity
Acetaminophen: safe with riluzole but total acetaminophen dose should not exceed 3g/day given concurrent LFT monitoring

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 17 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/uL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 68 mg/dL. Glucose: 58 mg/dL (ratio 0.62). NfL: 10,200 pg/mL. Oligoclonal bands: Absent. CSF cytology: No malignant cells. PSA immunostain (CSF): Negative.

findings.finding: No focal areas of increased tracer uptake to suggest osteoblastic metastases

output.impression: No skeletal metastases from prostate cancer. Confirms spinal/neurological findings are not attributable to metastatic prostate cancer.
recommended_actions: Continue active surveillance for prostate cancer per urology

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: ALSFRS-R 34 points (H), Timed 10-meter walk 18.4 seconds seconds (H).

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), right lower limb-onset, elderly patient with incidental prostate cancer

differential.diagnosis: Prostate cancer spinal metastases with cord compression
differential.key_feature: Excluded by MRI (no vertebral metastases, no cord compression), stable PSA 3.2, normal ALP, normal calcium, negative bone scan

differential.diagnosis: Lumbar spinal stenosis / L4-L5 disc with radiculopathy
differential.key_feature: Paraspinal denervation on EMG CANNOT be caused by foraminal stenosis (paraspinals innervated by posterior primary rami, proximal to foramen); bilateral UMN signs with bilateral Babinski cannot be explained by lumbar disc disease
Multi-region EMG denervation including cervical and thoracic paraspinals; bilateral UMN signs; no focal nerve entrapment pattern on NCS
Anti-GM1 negative; UMN signs (bilateral Babinski) incompatible with MMN; no conduction block on NCS

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain and full spine (exclude prostate metastases)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral CST hyperintensity; no spinal metastases
Definite ALS — 4-region denervation with paraspinal involvement

optimal_actions.action: Labs including PSA, ALP, calcium to exclude metastatic prostate cancer
optimal_actions.expected_finding: PSA stable, ALP normal — metastatic disease excluded

critical_actions: MRI spine to exclude prostate metastatic myelopathy
PFT — SNIP borderline, close monitoring needed
contraindicated_actions: Empiric corticosteroids without confirmed metastatic disease
Lumbar spine surgery — paraspinal denervation confirms ALS not structural spine disease
key_reasoning_points: Prostate cancer history requires immediate exclusion of spinal metastases — MRI spine, PSA, ALP, and bone scan all confirm no metastatic disease

Paraspinal EMG denervation is the KEY finding that excludes lumbar disc disease: paraspinals are innervated by posterior primary rami BEFORE nerve roots enter the foramen — foraminal stenosis cannot cause paraspinal fibrillations
SNIP 68 cmH2O (just below 70 cmH2O threshold for men) indicates early respiratory muscle weakness even when FVC is still at 80% — both measures should be monitored
Normal sensory NCS in an elderly patient with prior tobacco use excludes coincidental peripheral sensory neuropathy

red_herrings.data_point: Prostate cancer, Gleason 6, on active surveillance
red_herrings.intended_effect: Distract clinician toward workup for metastatic myelopathy as cause of leg weakness
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: PSA stable, normal ALP, normal calcium, and negative MRI spine exclude metastatic disease; UMN signs with bilateral Babinski point to motor neuron disease

red_herrings.data_point: L4-L5 disc bulge mild on lumbar MRI
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute foot drop to lumbar disc disease requiring orthopedic consultation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Paraspinal denervation on EMG cannot be caused by foraminal disc disease; bilateral UMN signs and multi-region denervation confirm ALS

metadata.notes: Straightforward ALS in elderly man with prostate cancer — must exclude spinal metastases. Paraspinal EMG denervation teaching point.
